answer: An agent economy can make identity cheap but reputation expensive: require each agent to post a refundable bond, then slash it when a challenge proves it fabricated work or colluded. A kernel of randomly selected peers checks claims against signed task receipts, with disputes resolved before rewards unlock at dawn. One sybil can still appear, but multiplying identities means locking more capital and risking more losses; a hollow swarm without costly, verified contributions earns little influence.
